goal: Convert finite-world ambiguity into an explicit experiment-design problem: choose the smallest admissible intervention set that separates all currently passive-equivalent worlds, or report that the intervention library is insufficient.

fixed_information.passive_signature: complete BAM state tuple (A mask, B mask, M mask, full M first-arrival vector)
fixed_information.unresolved_unit: unordered world pair sharing the same passive signature

intervention_library.outcome: binary long-corridor target reachability from v2.3
the already-known passive state signature; expected to split zero unresolved pairs

planner_contract.ranking_metric: number of currently unresolved world pairs split by the intervention
planner_contract.secondary_metric: largest residual equivalence-class size after adding the intervention
planner_contract.minimum_set_solver: exact exhaustive subset search over the finite intervention library

hypotheses.claim: A selected intervention set identifies every world within the passive finite universe if and only if every passive-unresolved world pair differs on at least one selected intervention outcome.
hypotheses.rule: Any disagreement between pair coverage and augmented-signature injectivity refutes E1.

hypotheses.claim: In the frozen v2.3 universe, P_barrier_challenge and H_long_corridor_challenge each split exactly 8 of the 16 passive-unresolved pairs, while repeat_passive_state splits 0.
The exact minimum intervention set that makes all 64 frozen worlds uniquely identifiable is {P_barrier_challenge, H_long_corridor_challenge}, of size 2.
hypotheses.rule: Any smaller separating set, any different size-2 separating set, or failure of this set to separate all worlds refutes E3.

boundary: The planner optimizes separation inside a declared finite world universe; it does not prove that the universe contains biological truth.
The intervention library must be declared before outcome-dependent selection.
A non-separating library must return unresolved rather than inventing a new intervention after seeing outcomes.
